what_its_for: Perindopril is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and to reduce the risk of heart attack in people with stable coronary artery disease (blocked or narrowed heart arteries). Lowering blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth, with or without food. It is best to take it at the same time each day, preferably in the morning. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist tells you it is okay.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition and how your body responds. The usual starting dose for high blood pressure is 4 mg once daily, which may be increased to 8 mg once daily. For heart disease, the starting dose is usually 4 mg once daily for 2 weeks, then increased to 8 mg once daily if tolerated. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store perindopril at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid using salt substitutes or potassium supplements unless your doctor tells you it is okay, as this medicine can raise potassium levels in your blood. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can further lower your blood pressure and increase dizziness. Be careful when rising quickly from a sitting or lying position to avoid dizziness or fainting. Avoid becoming dehydrated — drink enough fluids, especially in hot weather or during exercise. Talk to your doctor before taking any anti-inflammatory pain relievers (like ibuprofen or naproxen), as they can reduce how well this medicine works and may harm your kidneys.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or call emergency services (911) if you experience: sudden swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (this is called angioedema and can be life-threatening); difficulty breathing or swallowing; severe dizziness or fainting; signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness or irregular heartbeat; signs of kidney problems such as little or no urination, or swelling in your legs or feet; a dry, persistent cough that bothers you (this is a common side effect — your doctor may switch you to a different medicine); signs of infection such as fever or sore throat; or if you think you might be pregnant.
when_it_works: You may start to feel the effects of perindopril within a few hours of your first dose, but it may take 1 to 2 weeks of regular use to see the full benefit for blood pressure. For heart protection, the benefits build up over time with continued use. Even if you feel well, keep taking this medicine every day as directed — high blood pressure often has no symptoms.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby, especially in the second and third trimesters. Tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant while taking this medicine. Breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding, as it is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Elderly (65 and older): Older adults may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects and may need a lower starting dose. Kidney disease: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you more closely if you have kidney problems. Children: This medicine is generally not recommended for children unless specifically prescribed by a doctor.
